Site Statistics

mex0001 7.987 km² 13.24 km 3553.62 km 324.04 km 0.0793

This dataset contains 133 transects associated with the shoreline at site mex0001 . Each transect represents a segment of the coastline for which elevation and positional data have been analysed to estimate shoreline change trends and related metrics.

The orientation of transects spans from 215.277 ° to 228.857 °, with a mean orientation of 220.247 °, indicating the general alignment of shoreline segments within this site.

Note: Orientation data is not available for this site.

In terms of shoreline change:

  • The average linear trend across all transects is 2.253 m/year, with individual values ranging from 1.482 to 6.786 , suggesting a net accretional trend overall.

  • The Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of the trend model averages 18.283 m, indicating the typical deviation between observed points and the fitted trend line.

Note: Trend analysis data is not available for this site. This may indicate insufficient temporal data for trend calculations.

Confidence intervals on shoreline position trends are also available:

  • The mean lower bound is 0.071 , and the mean upper bound is 0.091 , reflecting the uncertainty range around trend estimates.

The number of valid data points per transect ( n_points_nonan ) ranges from 460 to 534 , with an average of 517.805 .

Site Zone Analysis

Site Zone Configuration

No areas of interest (AOIs) were identified for this site. This may be due to the min_zone_length ( ) parameter being set too high, or the transect data not meeting the criteria for any defined zones.

This site has been divided in to 1 zones consisting of at minimum 13 transects each. To increase or decrease the sensitivity of the zone definitions (i.e. the number of transects required to define a zone), you can adjust the min_zone_length parameter in the run_narrative_zoning function call above. Zone definitions are customisable, and extensible, and can be modified and extended by editing the aoi_definitions dictionary in the run_narrative_zoning function call above. Zone definitions applied to this site can be found in section Area of Interest Definitions at the bottom of this report.

Time Delimited Analysis

From January 01, 2010 to December 31, 2015

Data Processing

The analysis began with the complete satellite-derived shoreline dataset containing 540 temporal observations across 133 shore-normal transects. After applying the specified date range filter from January 01, 2010 to December 31, 2015 , the dataset was reduced to 110 observations spanning from January 2010 to December 2015 .

Analysis Results

We started with the full satellite-derived shoreline dataset: 540 time-stamped observations across 133 shore-normal transects. Limiting the window from January 01, 2010 to December 31, 2015 left 110 observations. These observations span 5.9 years, with an average of 104.9 data points per transect.

The time-bounded analysis reveals an average shoreline change rate of -0.26 meters per year across all analyzed transects. Individual transect trends ranged from -5.62 to 4.87 meters per year. The analysis processed a total of 13952 valid shoreline observations across all transects during the specified period.

The quality of the linear regression models is reflected in an average R² value of 0.14 , representing the proportion of variance in shoreline position explained by calculated trend.

Comparison

The original analysis, based on the complete temporal record, included 133 transects with an average trend of 2.25 meters per year (ranging from 1.48 to 6.79 meters per year).

The time-bounded analysis shows 133 transects with an average trend of -0.26 meters per year (ranging from -5.62 to 4.87 meters per year). This represents a 111.6% decrease in average trend magnitude compared to the historical baseline.

Model quality also differs between approaches: the time-bounded analysis achieved an average R² of 0.14 compared to 0.58 for the full dataset. This suggests the time-bounded period shows lower model reliability, indicating less consistent shoreline behavior during the specified timeframe.

Analysis Limitations

Time-bounded analysis could not be performed for this site within the specified date range. This may be due to insufficient satellite observations, data quality constraints, or the selected time period falling outside the available data coverage. The standard analysis using the full temporal dataset remains available above.

Sardinia time bounded analysis not currently supported

Narrative Generation Configuration

Area of Interest Definitions

The area of interest (AOI) definitions are used to categorise shoreline segments based on their trends and characteristics. Each AOI has a priority, conditions for classification, and a description template for narrative generation. This report returns zones with, at minimum, 13 transects.

AOI Name Priority Conditions
No Data 1 If the `trend` of the intersect is null.
Rapid Erosion 2 If the `trend` of the intersect is less than -0.8.
Moderate Erosion 3 If the `trend` of the intersect is less than -0.3.
Rapid Accretion 4 If the `trend` of the intersect is greater than 0.8.
Moderate Accretion 5 If the `trend` of the intersect is greater than 0.3.
High Uncertainty 6 If the `r2_score` of the intersect is less than 0.05. If the `rmse` of the intersect is greater than 30.
Steep Beach 7 If the `beach_slope` of the intersect is greater than 0.08.
Low Energy 8 If the `beach_slope` of the intersect is less than 0.04.
Stable 9 –
